transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Thu Feb 26 2026 16:00 PST
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Sam (BlueNova CTO), Maya (BlueNova Platform), Daniel (BlueNova Security)

Summary: quick weekly POC sync. Focus on access, edge region tests, and security gating. Agreed to run additional latency runs and share network logs.

00:00 Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, is this still a good time?
00:06 Sam (BlueNova): yeah, all good. we've got Maya and Daniel here too.
00:11 Priya (Redwood SE): cool, i'll do a very quick recap of where we left off last week — we had the staging keys applied, gateway ingress tested, but we still saw a bit of jitter from the eu-west egress path.
00:26 Maya (BlueNova): that's right, we saw timeouts around the 2 to 3% mark when burst traffic hit. could be our NLB config or something upstream.
00:37 Alex (Redwood): ok, today we'll run the edge-region probe for eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1, and also verify KMS/key rotation settings. Jordan will follow up on docs.
00:48 Daniel (BlueNova): quick security note, we need to see proof of KMS integration pattern, plus audit log retention. we prefer 1 year for now, with option to extend.
00:58 Jordan (Redwood CSM): noted, i have the security pack link in the chat — i'll re-share.
01:10 Priya: i'm going to trigger a controlled load test now with our test harness. it will run three phases, prefix caching on/off, different seq lengths, and a small token mix to replicate clinical note embeddings.
01:26 Sam: one ask — can you also include a warm cache run? sometimes our traffic pattern is very bursty but with prefix reuse.
01:34 Priya: yes, warm-run included. i'll log the exact commands in the benchmark sheet.

02:10 [~2 minutes into test - background noise/typing]
02:43 Priya: okay initial run finished, p50 is around 82ms, p90 around 180ms for eu-west with caching enabled, p90 drops to ~125ms with cache warmed.
02:59 Maya: that's higher than we'd like. our SLT is p90 < 120ms for interactive features.
03:08 Alex: understood. two immediate levers: tune batch window and force placement to dedicated capacity, or use a lower-cost variant but closer region. any constraints?
03:25 Sam: prefer to avoid dedicated right away, cost team will push back. region move maybe ok if privacy/regulatory allows. we need to check data residency for eu customers.
03:36 Daniel: also want to confirm that logs don't cross into other tenants, especially during fallback. last time there was an ambiguous routing event reported.
03:47 Priya: yeah, that was likely our smart-routing fallback hitting a fallback model in another region. we'll add stricter routing tags for the pilot to prevent that.
03:58 Jordan: action — Priya will run with routing tags set to eu-only, and Maya will provide egress IPs so we can whitelist.

05:10 Priya: starting second test, this time KV cache disabled to isolate batching effects.
05:26 [~load test running noises/keyboard]
05:54 Priya: results: eu-west p50 95ms, p90 210ms without cache, ap-southeast p90 165ms with warm cache. interestingly the ap-south traffic is lower variance.
06:12 Maya: that suggests our peering to eu-west might be the noisy part. we'll pull VPC flow logs and share.
06:25 Daniel: will check for any NAT gateway throttling or AWS side limits, also confirm the NLB cross-zone is enabled.
06:40 Alex: good. on the security doc — Daniel, do you need a whitepaper on how Redwood handles key wrapping and HSM?
06:48 Daniel: yes please, and a short runbook describing revocation steps if a key is rotated mid-pilot. we also want an audit sample showing request IDs and tokenization scrub.
07:05 Jordan: i'll attach the SOC2 attestation and a sample audit CSV, but for KMS/HSM specifics i'll loop in our security eng.
07:18 Priya: aside from latency, we caught a couple of model version mismatches in the staging logs — a recipe issue where the client pinned model v2.1 but the runtime was on v2.0-rc. that created slightly different tokenization.
07:36 Maya: oof, that explains some of the inference variance we logged. we'll standardize the model pin in our config and clear the cache.
07:45 Priya: perfect. also FYI, the transport layer had a few TLS handshake retries; looks like a client-side cipher mismatch on an older Java runtime we saw in one pod.
07:58 Sam: we'll push a patch to the runtime containers this week.

09:10 Alex: ok, switching to onboarding and creds: Maya, have you completed the service account role mapping?
09:18 Maya: almost — got IAM role with limited S3, but haven't confirmed the assume-role policy with our security team.
09:25 Alex: to be able to connect to private deployment we need: service account + role, KMS policy, and Peering/VPN. once those are in place we can open the pilot on dedicated staging.
09:38 Daniel: can you confirm whether Redwood stores any long-lived tokens in the control plane? we prefer ephemeral tokens only.
09:46 Priya: control plane stores no plaintext long-lived tokens; we use short-lived signed tokens and KMS envelope encryption for any secrets. docs in the security pack outline the flow but i'll send a summary.
09:59 Daniel: good. send that along.

12:02 Alex: quick check on fallback strategy — if we hit capacity, we'll route to a smaller model in-region. is that acceptable for your use-case for now?
12:13 Sam: yes as long as we fail gracefully and have a clear SLA and metrics for quality degradation. we need a rollback plan if hallucinations spike.
12:24 Priya: we'll enable quality monitoring tied to prompt sets — and set an alert if regeneration rate or hallucination proxies exceed thresholds.
12:35 Maya: can you send sample alert thresholds? we want to make sure we don't get paged for noise.
12:42 Priya: sure, default suggestion p95 regen rate < 3%, halluc proxy score < 0.07, but we can tune. i'll put suggestions in the sheet.

15:00 [mid-call recap]
15:06 Alex: recap: Priya will run edge probes with routing tags and upload results, Maya will provide VPC logs and confirm assume-role policy, Jordan will send security artifacts, Alex will send pricing.
15:22 Sam: timeline — we aim to decide on dedicated vs hosted pilot by next Wed 2026-03-04.

15:45 Daniel: one more security ask — can Redwood support customer-managed CMK in KMS? we need to hold key material for compliance.
15:58 Priya: yes, we support customer-managed CMKs. there's a small integration checklist but it's supported both in hosted and private modes.
16:12 Daniel: ok please document any caveats.

17:00 Priya: running final validation test — this one simulates bursty interactive traffic with 256 token prompts.
17:40 Priya: results at the end of that run: p50 78ms eu-west, p90 140ms with warm cache, cpu spikes on a couple of pods noticed; likely from our batch size hitting 64.
17:58 Maya: can you reduce batch size to 32 for the next run? we prefer lower tail latency even if cost is a touch higher.
18:06 Priya: yep will do.

19:30 Alex: paperwork/contract question — once the pilot passes, what procurement steps do you expect? Sam: we'll need a one-page SOW and a PO, plus legal review (2 weeks typical) — so speed matters if we want to launch by April.
19:52 Alex: understood. i'll include a sample SOW when i send pricing.
20:05 Jordan: i'll also include the escalation contacts and CSM onboarding plan.

22:00 [closing remarks]
22:08 Sam: thanks everyone. good progress.
22:12 Alex: thank you — we'll follow up with the benchmark CSV and security pack links. next sync same time next week?
22:20 Maya: yes works for us.
22:24 Daniel: we'll set aside time for the deeper security dive after you send the KMS runbook.

Notes/links shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/benchmarks-csv (benchmark sheet), https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/blue-nova (security pack), SSO SAML guide (doc link)

End of transcript.
